title: The .class File Format: Header, Constant Pool, Fields, and Methods
summary: How javac turns Java source into a structured binary .class file — magic number and version in the header, the constant pool's table of symbolic references, access flags, and how fields and methods are laid out for the JVM to load and execute.

references.label: The class File Format — Java Virtual Machine Specification, SE 25

title: JIT Compilation and Tiered Compilation: C1, C2, and Warm-Up
summary: How the JVM compiles bytecode to native code while the program runs, why it waits for code to get "hot" before compiling it, and how tiered compilation combines a fast-starting compiler (C1) with a slower, smarter one (C2).

references.label: Scott Oaks, "Java Performance: The Definitive Guide", 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2020) — Chapter 4 "Working with the JIT Compiler", pp. 89-120
JEP 410: Remove the Experimental AOT and JIT Compiler

title: Choosing a Garbage Collector: Serial, Parallel, G1, ZGC, and Shenandoah
summary: How the JVM's generational collectors trade off pause time, throughput, and CPU overhead, and which one the JVM actually defaults to today versus what a 2020-era book assumes.

references.label: Scott Oaks, "Java Performance: The Definitive Guide", 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2020) — Chapter 5 "An Introduction to Garbage Collection", pp. 121-152, and Chapter 6 "Garbage Collection Algorithms", pp. 153-201
HotSpot Virtual Machine Garbage Collection Tuning Guide — Java SE 25

title: Heap Analysis and Reading OutOfMemoryError Correctly
summary: How to use heap histograms and heap dumps to find out what's consuming memory, and how to read the different flavors of OutOfMemoryError instead of just adding more heap.

references.label: Scott Oaks, "Java Performance: The Definitive Guide", 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2020) — Chapter 7 "Heap Memory Best Practices", "Heap Analysis" section, pp. 203-215

title: Thread Pool Sizing: CPU-Bound vs. I/O-Bound Workloads
summary: Why sizing a ThreadPoolExecutor for compute-bound work means matching the core count, sizing for I/O-bound work means far exceeding it, and which half of this problem virtual threads actually solved.

references.label: Scott Oaks, "Java Performance: The Definitive Guide", 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2020) — Chapter 9 "Threading and Synchronization Performance", pp. 268-278

title: Java Flight Recorder: Low-Overhead Production Profiling
summary: How JFR's event-based, sub-1%-overhead recording lets you profile a live production JVM continuously, and how to control it entirely from the command line.

references.label: Scott Oaks, "Java Performance: The Definitive Guide", 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2020) — Chapter 3 "A Java Performance Toolbox", "Java Flight Recorder", pp. 74-88
JDK Flight Recorder documentation — Java SE 25
